meta.title: Ch 17: Accounting and Technology — MCQ Bank
meta.description: Chapter-wise practice MCQs for Chapter 17 (Accounting and Technology).

questions.why: XBRL = eXtensible Business Reporting Language — tags financial data using taxonomies for machine-readable reporting (used in MCA/SEBI filings).
questions.trend: No dominant past-pattern signal; included for balanced coverage (AI judgement).
questions.probWhy: Lower likelihood but possible — tagged-technology definitions appear as one-mark freebies Included so a low-probability surprise cannot catch you cold.

mem.tip: XBRL = XML for reporting: taxonomy + instance document + viewer. The 'eXtensible' spelling wins free marks.

questions.q: In an ERP with continuous (real-time) audit, 'CAAT' techniques primarily replace:
o: Manual vouching of samples by automated full-population testing and analytics
questions.why: Computer-Assisted Audit Techniques allow testing 100% of transactions and anomaly screening; judgment (risk assessment, opinion) is NOT automated. Segregation of duties is a control design issue.
questions.trend: Core concept that appears in some avatar in most attempts under the new scheme (pattern estimate).
questions.probWhy: Realistic likelihood for Nov 2026 — the scope of automation vs judgment is a new-syllabus signature AI prediction, not a certainty.

mem.tip: CAATs grind the population; humans keep the judgment. Automation widens samples, never replaces scepticism.

questions.q: Robotic Process Automation (RPA) in accounting primarily automates:
o: High-volume, rules-based repetitive tasks like reconciliations data pulls
questions.why: RPA suits structured, repetitive, rule-driven tasks; it does not replace estimates/judgment; supervisory controls remain essential.
questions.trend: No dominant past-pattern signal; included for balanced coverage (AI judgement).
questions.probWhy: Lower likelihood but possible — new-syllabus buzzword one-markers Included so a low-probability surprise cannot catch you cold.

mem.tip: RPA copies-and-pastes at machine speed; it reads rules, not situations.

questions.q: For an entity using a distributed ledger for transaction records, an auditor should primarily consider:
o: Access controls, key management, governance of the DLT, and whether ITF controls or substantive analytics address the risks
questions.why: DLT shifts emphasis to cryptographic key management, access rights, node governance; audit responses use ITF controls/substantive analytics; the ledger's immutability doesn't remove risks of input fraud and key misuse.
questions.trend: No dominant past-pattern signal; included for balanced coverage (AI judgement).
questions.probWhy: Lower likelihood but possible — the emerging-tech questions in the objective paper Included so a low-probability surprise cannot catch you cold.

mem.tip: Unstoppable records, stoppable inputs — audit the keys, the gates and the governance, not the hype.

questions.q: In an integrated ERP (finance, sales, inventory on one DB), the key financial-reporting risk is:
o: Improper access rights letting one module override balances without controls
questions.why: Integration concentrates access risk — segregation across modules + audit trails matter more than file copies.
questions.trend: Core concept that appears in some avatar in most attempts under the new scheme (pattern estimate).
questions.probWhy: Realistic likelihood for Nov 2026 — systems-thinking in a new-syllabus chapter AI prediction, not a certainty.

mem.tip: One database means one door; control the doorman, not the paperwork.

questions.q: Benford's law in audit analytics tests:
o: Digit-frequency patterns to spot anomalous manipulated amounts
questions.why: Benford's expected leading-digit distribution flags anomalies in large datasets — an analytics technique in CAATs/new tech syllabus.
questions.trend: No dominant past-pattern signal; included for balanced coverage (AI judgement).
questions.probWhy: Lower likelihood but possible — the data-technique vocabulary Included so a low-probability surprise cannot catch you cold.

mem.tip: Real numbers misbehave in a particular way — fake ones behave too well.

o: The tagged facts for the entity
questions.why: XBRL = taxonomy (definitions/tags) + instance document (facts tagged); MCA/SEBI filings use prescribed Indian taxonomies.
questions.trend: No dominant past-pattern signal; included for balanced coverage (AI judgement).
questions.probWhy: Lower likelihood but possible — taxonomy-vs-instance distinction Included so a low-probability surprise cannot catch you cold.

mem.tip: The dictionary is the taxonomy; your tagged sentences are the instance.

questions.q: Use of AI/ML in the entity's books primarily changes the auditor's assessment of:
o: IT general controls and the reliability of the models/data feeding accounting (estimates)
questions.why: Management's AI-driven estimates push the auditor to test model governance, data quality and bias/monitoring controls + challenge assumptions.
questions.trend: No dominant past-pattern signal; included for balanced coverage (AI judgement).
questions.probWhy: Lower likelihood but possible — the model-risk vocabulary Included so a low-probability surprise cannot catch you cold.

mem.tip: Auditing an algorithm: check the training, not only the answers.

questions.topic: New syllabus — Accounting and Technology chapter
questions.q: The new scheme (applicable from May 2026) added 'Accounting and Technology' to Paper 1. Its syllabus content directly includes:
o: XBRL, ERP-based accounting systems, big-data analytics, AI/ML impacts on financial reporting, and technology's audit interface
questions.why: Structural syllabus addition: the chapter embeds accounting-technology themes (XBRL taxonomy/filings, ERP flows, analytics in reporting, AI in estimates) — expect ICAI to fuse them with measurement scenarios and with the P3 digital-audit chapter.
questions.trend: Documented syllabus/amendment change — applicability from May 2026 exam onwards per ICAI BoS announcement.
questions.probWhy: Realistic likelihood for Nov 2026 — newly-added chapters attract disproportionate early-attempt attention AI prediction, not a certainty.

mem.ti: TI: New syllabus — Accounting and Technology chapter
mem.tip: New chapter, first attempts: the examiner's showroom floor.

questions.q: XBRL improves financial reporting mainly by:
o: Tagging data so reports are machine-readable — prepared once, validated automatically, comparable and re-usable
questions.why: eXtensible Business Reporting Language = standardised tags: consistency from preparation to analysis, single-sourcing to many regulators, automatic checking of arithmetic and completeness — recognition rules remain with the standards.
questions.trend: Core concept that appears in some avatar in most attempts under the new scheme (pattern estimate).
questions.probWhy: Realistic likelihood for Nov 2026 — machine-readable is not machine-audited AI prediction, not a certainty.

mem.tip: Numbers that travel are numbers anyone can check — faster.

questions.q: India's e-invoicing regime for notified taxpayers requires invoices to be:
o: Registered with the Invoice Registration Portal, which authenticates an Invoice Reference Number and QR code that the GST system reuses
questions.why: DOCUMENTED regime mechanics: the invoice is submitted to the IRP, returned authenticated with an IRN + QR; the same structured data pre-populates GST returns. Thresholds phase in by notification — verify the current limit for the attempt year.
questions.trend: Traceable to a real, publicly-notified amendment/standard (documented fact), tested in ICAI style.
questions.probWhy: Realistic likelihood for Nov 2026 — the IRN stamps the memo and the trail AI prediction, not a certainty.

mem.tip: The state becomes a notary inside every invoice footer.

questions.q: The payroll master file accepts a negative salary with no approval — in technology auditing this finding hits:
o: Application/input controls within the accounting system (and the ITGC chapter of the ICFR report)
questions.why: Validation edits on master files are application controls; their absence makes payroll figures unprovable — the same gap reappears in internal audit, systems audit and ICFR carve-outs.
questions.trend: Core concept that appears in some avatar in most attempts under the new scheme (pattern estimate).
questions.probWhy: Realistic likelihood for Nov 2026 — the system's edit is the accountant's control AI prediction, not a certainty.

mem.tip: A form that accepts nonsense manufactures it at scale.

questions.q: A bot that copies invoice fields from PDFs into the ERP following fixed rules is best described as:
o: Robotic process automation — rules-driven execution of repetitive tasks (OCR feeding scripted steps)
questions.why: RPA automates deterministic keystrokes; it learns nothing — audit consequence: transposition risk drops once the bot is controlled, and the bot's logic and change management are tested like any application control.
questions.trend: No dominant past-pattern signal; included for balanced coverage (AI judgement).
questions.probWhy: Lower likelihood but possible — bots follow scripts; models learn patterns Included so a low-probability surprise cannot catch you cold.

mem.tip: Automation repeats mistakes at machine speed until controls teach it to repeat accuracy.
